chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjaj, from Thalabah, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
And that which indicates what we mentioned earlier, namely that they are distinguished upon seeing the blood from the third menstruation, is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْأَطْهَارُ: The purities (referring to the state of being pure from major ritual impurity)
key_terms.الْأَقْرَاءُ: The menstruations (plural of qara', referring to the periods of bleeding)

ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence define the relationship between menstruation and ritual purity according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from the chain of al-Hajjāl and Thalabah clarifies that 'al-aqra'' refers specifically to the days of pure blood, which serve as the definitive markers for the end of the menstrual state. It establishes a critical legal distinction where the third menstruation is identified by the visible presence of blood, thereby providing a concrete criterion for women to determine their ritual purity status in accordance with the teachings of Imam al-Sadiq.
